source.title: Code Generation Tools (Almost) for Free? A Study of Few-Shot, Pre-Trained Language Models on Code
source.authors: Patrick Bareiss; Beatriz Souza; Marcelo d'Amorim; Michael Pradel

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream code-generation effectiveness for two Codex model sizes. This bears on downstream performance and scale, but it does not measure pretraining loss or reproduce the original scaling-law fits.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes for code mutation, oracle generation, and test generation, including results from a smaller Codex model. Only the model-size comparisons bear on V6. Results comparing FSLM tools with Major, MeMo, or Randoop, prompt variants, and cited scaling-law findings do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: RQ3 compares two Codex API models, Davinci (larger) and Cushman (smaller), on three few-shot Java code-generation tasks. This gives the direction of a downstream size effect bearing on V6 in a new setting. It reports no parameter counts, no pretraining loss and no scale curve, so the 'predictable' part of V6 cannot be assessed.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that a larger model improves effectiveness, or at least does not hurt it, on all three tasks, with a small effect for oracle generation. They recommend choosing model size per task given compute cost.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares few-shot downstream code-generation outcomes for two Codex model sizes; it does not fit or evaluate held-out pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The downstream model-size effect varies by task: it is clearer for code mutation and test generation, and small for oracle generation.
record.problems: Only two model sizes are compared, with no stated parameter counts or pretraining-loss measurements, so no general scaling curve or prediction from smaller runs can be evaluated. The authors also note that they do not compare across different models except by size. Results concern Java-based code-generation tasks.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant model-size results left out. Other per-project and per-method results compare tasks or tools, not model sizes.

untested.parts: Predictability of downstream performance from scale or from pretraining loss. Only two models of unstated size are compared, with no curve, no fit and no loss.

missing.what: Overlap of generated mutants with Major for the small model, 15.4% vs 18.4% for Davinci; also the shift in the kind-of-transformation distribution between the two models

record.verdict_notes: This is a two-point comparison of API models whose parameter counts are not stated, and Cushman is described as a derivative of a smaller model, so differences may not be due to size alone. The evidence on V6 is therefore directional only. Prompt-variant and tool-comparison results do not bear on any version. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and how it changes with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The study compares only two named model sizes and does not report a scale curve, pretraining loss, or predictions across a broad range of sizes.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices or setup.

rows.subject: Codex “Davinci”

rows.note: Davinci is the larger of the two compared models.
rows.check: Total mutants generated (2,721 vs 2,487) is a volume measure, not a quality measure. Model sizes are unstated, and Cushman is a derivative model, so size is not the only difference.

relationships.condition: Code mutation and test case generation, Codex Davinci vs the smaller Cushman
relationships.reason: The larger model generates more mutants (r1), more compilable mutants (62.5% vs 53.8%, r3) and higher line coverage (14% vs 10%, r7). This supports the direction only.
relationships.display_finding: Davinci generated more mutants than Cushman, increased compilable mutants from 53.8% to 62.5%, and raised line coverage from 10% to 14%.

relationships.condition: Test oracle generation, Codex Davinci vs Cushman
relationships.reason: The size gain is negligible (F1 0.60 vs 0.58); the authors call the results nearly identical (r5).
relationships.display_finding: F1 differs only slightly at 0.60 versus 0.58, with the results described as nearly identical.
